subject: hedgehogs
one_liner: A generative image studio for the discerning nocturnal insectivore. Prompt by snout. Render by moonlight. Ship nothing before dusk.
brand_voice_notes: Dry, faux-corporate, fully committed. Bramble talks like a frontier AI lab that has accepted hedgehog biology as a set of enterprise requirements: snout-based input is 'multimodal', hibernation is a billing quarter, and predator avoidance is a safety layer. Never winks. Treats an 11% prompt accuracy rate as a benchmark victory.

hero.sub: Bramble turns snout input into gallery-grade renders of leaf piles, hedgerows, and open compost bins. Overnight. While you were up anyway.

features.title: Snout-native prompting
features.blurb: A pressure-sensitive input pad translates snuffling into structured prompts. Independent benchmarks put intent accuracy at 11%, which our benchmarks describe as state of the art. The other 89% of renders are damp leaves, which our users describe as fine.

features.title: Dusk-to-dawn rendering
features.blurb: Jobs queue at sunset and finish by sunrise, aligned to your circadian rhythm. Prompts submitted in daylight are discarded without notification, out of respect. Our GPUs also prefer it cooler.

features.title: Predator-negative by default
features.blurb: Every model ships with --no owls, --no badgers, --no traffic baked into the weights. This cannot be toggled in settings. Removing it requires a written waiver, a witness, and a second, braver hedgehog.

demo_screen_concept: A render-queue console styled like Bramble's prompt channel: a prompt bar with a snout-input toggle and live 'snuffle transcription' readout, a 2x2 grid of finished renders (damp leaf pile, hedgerow at dusk, moss bed, open compost bin) each with U1-U4 upscale and V1-V4 variation buttons, a queue sidebar listing pending jobs with a 'renders begin at dusk' countdown, and a GPU-weather status widget reporting cloud cover over the data burrow.

images.rationale: Demo is photo-shaped (the 2x2 render grid is literally the product's output), so the budget went there: 3 nocturnal renders (leaf pile, hedgerow, moss bed; the 4th grid slot stays a mid-render shimmer frame by design). 1 headshot for the lead testimonial; the other two testimonial slots deliberately show 'portrait queued' render frames, on-bit. Hero image skipped: typographic aurora hero whose render grid reuses the demo assets.

design_direction.style: Moonlit generative-atelier, aurora glass dark mode. The page is staged as the launch site of a frontier AI lab that has decided the hedgehog is an underserved creative and files foraging under generative practice. A deep nocturnal indigo ground (#0F1220) runs the whole page under two slow-drifting radial aurora washes (moonbeam lilac and moss green at low alpha, 30s drift loops), the first gradients this studio has permitted in a week. Panels are frosted glass: rgba fills at 6-8% white, 1px lilac-alpha hairline borders, 16px radii, backdrop-filter blur(14px), a faint inner top highlight, so every card reads as condensation on a window the hedgehog is renting. The core motif is the render frame: a 1:1 rounded frame with animated corner ticks and a scan-line shimmer that sweeps once on reveal, wrapping every generated image, empty queue slot, and testimonial headshot, so all content reads as model output awaiting review. The second motif is the moon-phase meter: an eight-dot lunar cycle used as progress bar, list bullet, and pricing-tier badge, always rendered mid-waning. One moonbeam lilac (#B79CFF) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, prompt-bar focus rings, and one italicized word per headline; one rationed moss green (#A3C585) is reserved strictly for live telemetry (the dusk countdown, GPU-weather status, verified-insectivore badges) and appears nowhere else. Fraunces sets the wordmark and headlines in soft wonky serif with research-lab-that-raised-too-much confidence; Outfit carries plain, faintly model-card body copy. Every figure that pretends to be render telemetry (queue depths, snuffle accuracy percentages, seed numbers, tier prices) is set in Fira Code with tabular figures inside inset indigo wells, so it reads like the job log, not marketing. Motion is nocturne-restrained: auroras drift on 30s loops, render frames shimmer once on reveal, corner ticks blink on hover, the moon meter wanes one dot on scroll, CTAs glow softly on hover and depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No daylight mode, no print chrome, no hairline editorial rules, no offset sticker shadows, no catalog borders, no HUD brackets, no storefront capsules, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files instinct under 'user-generated content' and considers the sun a scheduled outage.
design_direction.archetype: Frontier AI-lab creative-tool launch: aurora hero with monumental soft-serif headline and a live render-frame grid, prompt-bar motif repeated as section chrome, three glass feature cards, community-showcase testimonials in render frames, pricing as compute tiers with moon-phase badges, closing CTA band, handoff to the render-queue console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 30s aurora drift loops; one-shot scan-line shimmer on render-frame reveal; corner ticks blink on hover; moon-phase meter wanes on scroll; soft glow bloom on CTA hover with 1px press depression; 6px fade-up section entrances staggered 40ms; everything behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero: left, Fraunces headline with 'burrow' italicized in moonbeam lilac over a short model-card subline and the waitlist CTA; right, a 2x2 render-frame grid showing one finished render, one mid-shimmer slot, and two queued slots labeled in Fira Code (queued · begins at dusk), with the moss-green dusk countdown chip pinned to the grid corner. Aurora washes anchor behind the grid so the glass panels have something to blur.
